taxonomy.subtopic: CFTR-dependent ductal bicarbonate and water secretion

questions.stem_html: A 15-year-old boy with cystic fibrosis has poor weight gain and bulky, foul-smelling stools despite a high-calorie diet. After intravenous secretin, the accompanying diagram shows a markedly reduced rise in duodenal bicarbonate concentration. Which transport abnormality best explains both the test result and his pancreatic insufficiency?

options.text_html: Reduced sodium-glucose cotransport across the proximal small-intestinal brush border
Failure of pancreatic acinar cells to synthesize trypsinogen and chymotrypsinogen
Increased sodium-dependent bile acid uptake by terminal ileal enterocytes
Excessive cholecystokinin-mediated contraction of the sphincter of Oddi
Reduced apical CFTR-dependent chloride and bicarbonate conductance in pancreatic duct epithelial cells

questions.explanation_html: Pancreatic duct cells use CFTR to support chloride recycling and bicarbonate movement into the duct lumen. Bicarbonate and accompanying water create an alkaline, high-flow secretion that flushes acinar enzymes into the duodenum and neutralizes gastric acid. Loss of CFTR function produces scant, acidic, viscous secretions that obstruct ducts, damage exocrine tissue, and cause maldigestion and steatorrhea.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: Acinar enzyme production may decline after chronic duct obstruction, but the primary defect is impaired ductal ion and water secretion.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Terminal ileal bile acid uptake is unrelated to the secretin-stimulated pancreatic bicarbonate response.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Sodium-glucose cotransport affects carbohydrate and water absorption in enterocytes, not pancreatic duct alkalinization.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Sphincter of Oddi contraction does not explain the intrinsic low-bicarbonate secretion characteristic of CFTR dysfunction.

questions.educational_objective: CFTR loss in pancreatic duct epithelium reduces bicarbonate-rich fluid secretion, leading to acidic viscous secretions, duct obstruction, and exocrine pancreatic insufficiency.

media.alt_text: Original pancreatic duct cell diagram showing CFTR-supported chloride recycling, bicarbonate secretion, water movement, and the low-flow acidic secretion produced by CFTR loss.
